name: knowledge_update
description: Tests whether engram surfaces the CURRENT state of evolving facts, not stale versions. 20 events across 4 topics, each topic with an evolution arc: initial decision → refinement → revision/reversal. The queries ask for the current state. A system that returns the latest version passes; one that returns an earlier version (even if semantically closer to the query) fails. This scenario exposes the knowledge-update gap: engram has no mechanism to mark an older event as superseded by a newer one. Built 2026-04-10 to evaluate whether topic_key/upsert patterns (a la GP/engram) would add value.

events.text: We decided to use Redis as our caching layer because the in-process LRU cache was causing stale reads across 12 pods due to cache invalidation failures.
Updated the Redis cache configuration: TTL changed from 5 minutes to 60 seconds after observing that product prices were stale for too long during flash sales.
Reverted from Redis back to in-process caching with Caffeine. Redis added 3ms p99 latency per request and the flash sale staleness was solved by pub/sub invalidation instead of short TTLs.
Chose PostgreSQL 16 for the analytics warehouse because we need write concurrency above 200 connections per second and SQLite cannot handle that.
Added TimescaleDB extension on top of PostgreSQL for the analytics warehouse. Hypertable partitioning reduced query times from 12 seconds to 400ms on the daily aggregation dashboard.
Migrated the analytics warehouse from PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB to ClickHouse. The write throughput at 500K events per second exceeded what TimescaleDB could handle even with hypertables.
Implemented OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for mobile clients after API keys were found leaking in client-side JavaScript bundles.
Added device fingerprinting to the OAuth flow. Tokens are now bound to device_id and refresh tokens are rejected if the device fingerprint changes.
Replaced OAuth 2.0 PKCE with passkey-based authentication using WebAuthn. The OAuth refresh token rotation was causing session drops on iOS when the app was backgrounded for more than 15 minutes.
Set up canary deployments with ArgoCD. Each release rolls out to 5 percent of traffic first and auto-reverts if error rate exceeds 1 percent during a 10-minute bake window.
Extended the canary bake window from 10 to 30 minutes after a latent memory leak only manifested after 20 minutes of traffic. Also added memory usage as a canary gate metric.

Switched from percentage-based canary to header-based routing. Internal team gets the canary via X-Canary header for 24 hours before any customer traffic is shifted. This caught the Stripe webhook regression that the 30-minute bake missed.
Daily standup: cache team reports Redis migration on track, no blockers. Database team finalizing TimescaleDB benchmarks.
Sprint review: auth flow redesign approved by security team. Deploy pipeline improvements merged to main.
Retrospective action item: improve canary deployment documentation for on-call engineers.
Planning session: next sprint focuses on cache layer optimization and database migration tooling.
Ticket INFRA-2847 created: investigate Redis memory usage spike on production cluster node 3.
Ticket AUTH-1523 resolved: OAuth token refresh endpoint returning 500 intermittently due to connection pool exhaustion.
Ticket DB-892 in progress: TimescaleDB continuous aggregate refresh failing on large partitions.
Ticket DEPLOY-456 closed: ArgoCD sync timeout increased from 5 to 15 minutes for large Helm charts.
